title: Register study on a of anti-infectives concentrations in clinical routine
summary:
This study involves setting up a registry to collect treatment data from patients who are being treated with certain anti-infective drugs. The aim of the study is to investigate whether the desired concentrations of these drugs are achieved in the blood and at what point this occurs.

In addition, the study will examine whether there are patients who are at increased risk of having drug levels that are too low or too high. Various influencing factors will be taken into account, such as individual physical characteristics (e.g., severe obesity or impaired kidney function) and special treatment procedures such as dialysis or extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO).

This will provide a better understanding of which patients would particularly benefit from regular monitoring of drug levels.
conditions: Patients with infectious diseases who are being treated with anti-infective agents.

interventions.name: This study aims to create a structured, prospective registry to investigate whether and when defined target ranges are achieved in patients undergoing therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) of anti-infectives and whether patients who are at risk of reaching sub- or supratherapeutic ranges can be identifi

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with routine TDM of anti-infective
Exclusion criteria:
Routine TDM of drugs that are not part of ATC class J01-J05
